source.text: Ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα μὴ σκανδαλισθῆτε.

records.literal_gloss: These things I have spoken to you so that not you may be caused to stumble.

en.L: These things I have spoken to you so that you may not be caused to stumble.
en.B: I have told you all this so that you will not stumble and fall away.
en.R: I am telling you this so that you will not stumble and fall away.

es.L: Estas cosas {{plural_you:les|os}} he hablado para que no {{plural_you:tropiecen|tropecéis}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he dicho todo esto para que no {{plural_you:tropiecen y se aparten|tropecéis y os apartéis}} de la fe.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo esto para que no {{plural_you:tropiecen ni se aparten|tropecéis ni os apartéis}} de la fe.

fr.L: Ces choses, je vous les ai dites afin que vous ne soyez pas amenés à trébucher.
fr.B: Je vous ai dit tout cela pour que vous ne trébuchiez pas et n’abandonniez pas la foi.
fr.R: Je vous dis cela pour que vous ne trébuchiez pas et que vous n’abandonniez pas la foi.

sw.B: Nimewaambia mambo haya yote ili msijikwae mkaiacha imani.
sw.R: Ninawaambia mambo haya ili msijikwae na kuiacha imani yenu.

vi.L: Ta đã nói những điều này với các con để các con không bị vấp ngã.
vi.B: Ta đã nói với các con mọi điều này để các con không vấp ngã mà lìa bỏ đức tin.
vi.R: Ta nói cho các con biết điều này để các con không vấp ngã và bỏ niềm tin.

ko.L: 내가 이것들을 너희에게 말한 것은 너희가 걸려 넘어지지 않게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 너희에게 이 모든 것을 말한 것은, 너희가 걸려 넘어져 떨어져 나가지 않게 하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 이 말을 하는 것은, 너희가 걸려 넘어져서 믿음을 저버리지 않게 하려는 것이다.

decisions.choice: be caused to stumble: be tripped up so as to fall away from faith
alternatives: be offended, have one's feelings hurt
decisions.reason: The verb σκανδαλισθῆτε pictures a stumbling block that trips someone so that they fall. In John it means losing hold of faith in Jesus, as when many disciples turned back after the hard words of 6:61, 66, where the same verb is used. Here the danger is the hatred and persecution just described: if it took them by surprise, they might give up.

decisions.choice: these things I have spoken: the warnings of 15:18-27 about the world's hatred
alternatives: the whole of the farewell talk
decisions.reason: "These things" looks back to what Jesus has just said about the world hating and persecuting them (15:18-25), and forward to the plain warning of verse 2. The same opening recurs through the talk (14:25; 15:11; 16:4, 25, 33). The perfect tense presents the warning as given and standing.

decisions.choice: stumble and fall away
decisions.reason: "Stumble" keeps the picture of the verb, as at 6:61, and "fall away" says what the picture means here (meaning decision m1). "Be offended" now means having one's feelings hurt, which is far too weak.

decisions.choice: tropiecen y se aparten de la fe (B); tropiecen ni se aparten de la fe (R)
decisions.reason: "Tropezar" keeps the picture of the verb, as at 6:61, and "apartarse de la fe" says what the picture means here (meaning decision m1). "Escandalizarse" now usually means being shocked, which is far too weak.

decisions.choice: speech tenses: passé composé for the Greek perfects and aorists ("je vous ai dit"), present and future as in the Greek, at every level
alternatives: passé simple for the past tenses of speech
decisions.reason: This passage (16:1-15) is all Jesus's speech, so it has no narrative tense to settle; inside speech every level uses the passé composé, as people speak and as the rest of John's French does (see 1:19). Readable uses the present "je vous dis cela", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: trébucher (L); trébucher et abandonner la foi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb pictures a stumbling block that trips someone so that they fall away from faith (meaning decision m1). French "être scandalisé" now means being shocked or outraged, which misses the sense; "trébucher" keeps the picture, and Balanced and Readable add what it means, as the English adds "fall away".

decisions.choice: msikwazwe (L); msijikwae mkaiacha imani (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "kukwaza" (to trip someone up), the verb used for the same Greek word at 6:61. Balanced and Readable say "stumble" with "kujikwaa" and add what the picture means here, giving up faith (meaning note m1), as the English does. "Kuchukizwa" (be offended) is far too weak.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (mimi, yangu, yeye, kwake, mwenyewe)
decisions.reason: As in the earlier chapters: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb (niliwaambia, nitamtuma), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so this passage has fewer spans than the English. Free pronouns and possessives for Jesus, the Father and the Spirit carry the setting; one at the start of a sentence is written plain with its capital.

decisions.choice: Jesus says "Ta" for himself and "các con" to the disciples
decisions.reason: Vietnamese pronouns name the relationship. As the style guide sets for the whole book, Jesus speaks of himself as "Ta" (with the deity_pronoun setting mid-sentence) and addresses his disciples as "các con", a teacher speaking to those in his care; the disciples call him "Thầy" and themselves "chúng con".

decisions.choice: vấp ngã mà lìa bỏ đức tin (B); vấp ngã và bỏ niềm tin (R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "vấp ngã" alone can mean any moral slip; Balanced and Readable add the falling away from faith that the meaning decision gives.

decisions.choice: 걸려 넘어지다 (L); 걸려 넘어져 떨어져 나가다 (B); 걸려 넘어져서 믿음을 저버리다 (R)
decisions.reason: 걸려 넘어지다 keeps the picture of the Greek verb in plain modern Korean; 실족하다 is the older church word and less clear to new readers.

source.text: ἀποσυναγώγους ποιήσουσιν ὑμᾶς· ἀλλ’ ἔρχεται ὥρα ἵνα πᾶς ὁ ἀποκτείνας ὑμᾶς δόξῃ λατρείαν προσφέρειν τῷ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Out-of-synagogue [ones] they will make you; but comes an hour that everyone the [one] having killed you will think service to offer to the God.

en.L: They will put you out of the synagogue; but an hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think [that {{gender:they are|he is}}] offering service to God.
en.B: They will expel you from the synagogue. In fact, an hour is coming when anyone who kills you will think {{gender:they are|he is}} doing God a sacred service.
en.R: They will throw you out of the synagogue. In fact, the time will come when anyone who kills you will think that {{gender:they are|he is}} serving God by doing it.

es.L: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} expulsarán de la sinagoga; pero viene una hora en que todo el que {{plural_you:los|os}} mate creerá ofrecer culto a Dios.
es.B: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} expulsarán de la sinagoga. Más aún, viene una hora en que cualquiera que {{plural_you:los|os}} mate creerá que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} está rindiendo a Dios un servicio sagrado.
es.R: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} expulsarán de la sinagoga. Y aún más: llegará la hora en que cualquiera que {{plural_you:los|os}} mate pensará que así sirve a Dios.

fr.L: Ils feront de vous des exclus de la synagogue ; mais vient une heure où quiconque vous tuera croira offrir un culte à Dieu.
fr.B: Ils vous excluront de la synagogue. Bien plus, l’heure vient où quiconque vous tuera croira accomplir pour Dieu un service sacré.
fr.R: Ils vous chasseront de la synagogue. Et même, le moment viendra où ceux qui vous tueront penseront servir Dieu en faisant cela.

sw.L: Watawatenga na sinagogi; lakini saa inakuja ambapo kila atakayewaua atadhani [kwamba] anamtolea Mungu ibada.
sw.B: Watawatenga na sinagogi. Zaidi ya hayo, saa inakuja ambapo yeyote atakayewaua atadhani kwamba anamtolea Mungu ibada takatifu.
sw.R: Watawafukuza kutoka sinagogi. Tena, wakati utakuja ambapo yeyote atakayewaua atadhani kwamba kwa kufanya hivyo anamtumikia Mungu.

vi.L: Họ sẽ đuổi các con ra khỏi nhà hội; nhưng giờ đang đến khi bất cứ ai giết các con sẽ nghĩ [rằng mình] đang dâng sự phụng thờ lên Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Họ sẽ trục xuất các con khỏi nhà hội. Hơn thế nữa, giờ đang đến khi ai giết các con cũng tưởng mình đang dâng lên Đức Chúa Trời một việc thờ phượng.
vi.R: Họ sẽ đuổi các con ra khỏi nhà hội. Thậm chí sẽ đến lúc ai giết các con cũng nghĩ làm vậy là phục vụ Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그들이 너희를 회당에서 쫓아낼 것이다. 그러나 너희를 죽이는 사람은 누구나 [자기가] 하나님께 섬김을 드린다고 생각할 때가 온다.
ko.B: 그들이 너희를 회당에서 내쫓을 것이다. 그뿐 아니라, 너희를 죽이는 사람마다 자기가 하나님께 거룩한 예배를 드리고 있다고 생각할 때가 온다.
ko.R: 사람들이 너희를 회당에서 쫓아낼 것이다. 그뿐 아니라, 너희를 죽이는 사람이 그렇게 하면서 하나님을 섬긴다고 생각할 때가 올 것이다.

decisions.choice: put out of the synagogue: shut out of the community's worship and common life
decisions.reason: The same word as in 9:22 and 12:42, found in the New Testament only in John. The synagogue was where Jews gathered for prayer and the reading of Scripture and the center of a town's shared life, so to be put out of it was to be cut off from one's own people. What the man born blind suffered (9:34) and the rulers feared (12:42), Jesus now foretells for his disciples.

decisions.choice: they: those who hate Jesus and his followers (15:18-25), here those with authority over the synagogue
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. It carries on the "they" of 15:20-25, the world that hates Jesus. Only those with authority over a synagogue could put people out of it, as the leaders had agreed to do in 9:22. The text does not say more about who they will be. The disciples themselves are Jews, and so is Jesus.

decisions.choice: offer service to God: perform an act of worship, a sacred duty offered to God
decisions.reason: The noun λατρείαν is used of the worship of God, above all the service of the temple and its sacrifices (Romans 9:4; Hebrews 9:1, 6), and the verb προσφέρειν is the word for offering a sacrifice. The killers will think that killing Jesus's followers is itself worship pleasing to God. Saul of Tarsus is an example: he persecuted the church out of zeal for God (Acts 26:9-11; Galatians 1:13-14; Philippians 3:6).

decisions.choice: but an hour is coming when: not merely that, but worse; a time set for this to happen
alternatives: the hour of Jesus's death and glory
decisions.reason: The "but" here heightens: not only exclusion, but death. "An hour is coming" is the phrase of 4:21 and 5:25, a time that will surely come. It is not Jesus's own hour (12:23; 13:1) but the time when his followers will suffer, which verse 4 calls "their hour". The word ἵνα, usually "so that", here means "when", as in 12:23 and 13:1.

decisions.choice: everyone who kills you ... [that {{gender:they are|he is}}] (L); anyone who kills you ... {{gender:they are|he is}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Everyone who kills" is general and in principle includes anyone; the pronoun that English needs after it carries the gender setting. Literal brackets the words the Greek leaves unstated.

decisions.choice: put out of (L); expel from (B); throw out of (R); hour (L, B); time (R); sacred service (B); serving God (R)
decisions.reason: Each level uses the wording it used at 9:22, so readers see the same word. Literal and Balanced keep "hour", as at 4:21 and 5:25; Readable says "time", because "hour" sounds like sixty minutes. "Sacred service" shows that the killers think of their deed as worship (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: expulsarán de la sinagoga (every level); hora (L, B, R); ofrecer culto (L); rendir un servicio sagrado (B); así sirve a Dios (R)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "expulsar de la sinagoga", the wording of 9:22 and 12:42. "Llega la hora" is natural Spanish for a time that will surely come, so Readable keeps "hora" as at 4:21. The killers think their deed is worship (meaning decision m3). "Todo el que" and "cualquiera que" are already general and need no pronoun after them, so there is no gender setting.

decisions.choice: quiconque vous tuera croira offrir (L, B); ceux qui vous tueront penseront servir (R); no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs a pronoun after "think", and that pronoun takes the gender setting. French, like the Greek, can follow "croire" and "penser" with an infinitive, so it needs no pronoun; "quiconque" and the plural "ceux qui" already take in anyone. Literal therefore needs no brackets either.

decisions.choice: feront de vous des exclus de la synagogue (L); vous excluront (B); vous chasseront (R); heure (L, B); moment (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek structure ("make you put-out-of-synagogue ones") with the noun "exclus"; Balanced and Readable use the plain verbs. The same word occurs at 9:22 and 12:42, which should use the same French at each level; a reviewer should compare them, since they were drafted separately. "Heure" keeps the phrase "une heure vient" of 4:21 and 5:25 at Literal and Balanced (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: watawatenga na sinagogi (L, B); watawafukuza kutoka sinagogi (R); anamtolea Mungu ibada (L, B)
decisions.reason: Each level uses its wording from 9:22 and 12:42 for being shut out of the synagogue community (meaning note m1). "Kumtolea Mungu ibada" keeps the language of offering worship (m3); Readable says plainly that they will think they are serving God. Literal and Balanced keep "saa" (hour), as at 4:21; Readable says "wakati". No gender span is needed: "yeyote" covers anyone.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "mình" (oneself)
alternatives: a gender setting as in the English
decisions.reason: The English needs a gender setting for "they are | he is". Vietnamese refers back with the reflexive "mình", which is neither male nor female, so no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: 자기 / 사람, with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean says "anyone who kills you" and "he himself" with 사람 and the reflexive 자기, which are already inclusive; the gender setting has nothing to change (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: 때 for "hour" at every level
decisions.reason: 때 is the Korean word for an appointed time; 시간 would read as clock time.

source.text: καὶ ταῦτα ποιήσουσιν ὅτι οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τὸν πατέρα οὐδὲ ἐμέ.

records.literal_gloss: And these things they will do because not they knew the Father nor me.

en.L: And these things they will do because they have not known the Father nor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: They will do these things because they have never known the Father or {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: They will do these things because they do not know the Father or {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Y estas cosas harán porque no han conocido al Padre ni a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: Harán estas cosas porque nunca han conocido al Padre ni a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Harán estas cosas porque no conocen al Padre, y tampoco {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conocen a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

fr.L: Et ces choses, ils les feront parce qu’ils n’ont connu ni le Père ni {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: Ils feront cela parce qu’ils n’ont jamais connu ni le Père ni {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Ils feront ces choses parce qu’ils ne connaissent pas le Père, et qu’ils ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaissent pas non plus.

sw.L: Na mambo haya watayatenda kwa sababu hawakumjua Baba wala {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.
sw.B: Watayatenda mambo haya kwa sababu hawajawahi kumjua Baba wala kunijua {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.
sw.R: Watafanya mambo haya kwa sababu hawamjui Baba, wala hawanijui {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.

vi.L: Và họ sẽ làm những điều này vì họ đã không biết Cha, cũng không [biết] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Họ sẽ làm những điều ấy vì họ chưa bao giờ biết Cha, cũng chẳng biết {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Họ sẽ làm những điều đó vì họ không biết Cha, cũng không biết {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 이런 일들을 할 것은 아버지도 나도 알지 못하였기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그들이 이런 일을 하는 것은 아버지도 나도 한 번도 알지 못했기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그들이 이런 일을 하는 것은 아버지도 나도 모르기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: the root of persecution: not knowing the Father, and so not knowing the Son
decisions.reason: Jesus said the same in 15:21 and told his opponents that they knew neither him nor his Father (7:28; 8:19, 54-55). Those who kill in God's name (verse 2) show that they do not know him; to know the Father is to know the one he sent (14:7; 17:3).

decisions.choice: have not known: they have never come to know them
alternatives: did not recognize them at a particular moment
decisions.reason: The past tense ἔγνωσαν looks at their whole relation to God and to Jesus: they never came to know them. This is a settled state, not one mistake.

decisions.choice: they will do (SBLGNT)
alternatives: they will do to you (many manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "to you" after "they will do", making plain who suffers, as 15:21 has it. Important early manuscripts lack it. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: have never known (B); do not know (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the settled state of the past tense with "never" (meaning decision m2). Readable uses the present, the plain way to say what is true of them now.

decisions.choice: nunca han conocido (B); no conocen (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced brings out the settled state of the past tense with "nunca" (meaning decision m2); Readable says plainly what is true of them now.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect is carried by the honorific -si-, 께서 and 그분 at every level (style guide section 7).

source.text: ἀλλὰ ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἡ ὥρα αὐτῶν μνημονεύητε αὐτῶν ὅτι ἐγὼ εἶπον ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: But these things I have spoken to you so that when comes the hour of them you may remember them, that I said to you.

en.L: But these things I have spoken to you so that when their hour comes you may remember them, that I told [them] to you.
en.B: But I have said these things to you so that when the hour for them comes, you will remember that I told you of them.
en.R: But I have warned you about these things, so that when they happen, you will remember that I told you.

es.L: Pero estas cosas {{plural_you:les|os}} he hablado para que, cuando llegue su hora, {{plural_you:se acuerden|os acordéis}} de ellas, de que yo {{plural_you:se las|os las}} dije.
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho estas cosas para que, cuando llegue la hora en que sucedan, {{plural_you:recuerden|recordéis}} que yo {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} había dicho.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} he advertido de estas cosas para que, cuando sucedan, {{plural_you:se acuerden|os acordéis}} de que yo {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} dije.

fr.L: Mais ces choses, je vous les ai dites afin que, quand leur heure viendra, vous vous souveniez d’elles, que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je vous [les] ai dites.
fr.B: Mais je vous ai dit ces choses pour que, lorsque l’heure en sera venue, vous vous souveniez que je vous en avais parlé.
fr.R: Mais je vous ai prévenus de ces choses pour que, quand elles arriveront, vous vous souveniez que je vous l’avais dit.

sw.L: Lakini mambo haya nimewaambia ili saa yake itakapofika myakumbuke, kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niliwaambia.
sw.B: Lakini nimewaambia mambo haya ili saa yake itakapofika, mkumbuke kwamba niliwaambia habari zake.
sw.R: Lakini nimewaonya juu ya mambo haya, ili yatakapotokea, mkumbuke kwamba niliwaambia.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói những điều này với các con, để khi giờ của chúng đến, các con nhớ lại chúng, rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con [rồi].
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói những điều này với các con, để khi giờ của chúng đến, các con nhớ rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã báo trước cho các con.
vi.R: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã báo trước cho các con những điều này, để khi chúng xảy ra, các con nhớ rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con rồi.

ko.L: 그러나 내가 이것들을 너희에게 말한 것은, 그 일들의 때가 오면 너희가 그것들을, 곧 내가 너희에게 [그것들을] 말했다는 것을 기억하게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 내가 이것을 너희에게 말하는 것은, 그 일들이 일어날 때가 오면 내가 그것을 너희에게 말해 주었다는 것을 너희가 기억하게 하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 이런 일들을 미리 알려 주는 것은, 그런 일이 실제로 일어날 때 내가 너희에게 말해 주었다는 것을 너희가 기억하게 하려는 것이다.

decisions.choice: their hour: the time when these things happen
alternatives: the hour of the persecutors, their time of power (compare Luke 22:53, "this is your hour")
decisions.reason: "Their" is plural and most naturally points back to "these things" at the start of the sentence, the same word as "them" in "remember them". The hour is the time foretold in verse 2. It could refer to the persecutors, whose "hour" would be the time they are allowed to act, but "these things" are the nearer and more likely antecedent.

decisions.choice: remember them, that I told you: remember that Jesus told them beforehand
decisions.reason: The Greek says "remember them, that I told you": the object is named first, then what about it is to be remembered. The "I" is emphatic: it was Jesus himself who warned them. When persecution comes, it will not shake their faith but confirm what he said, as in 13:19 and 14:29.

decisions.choice: the hour of them (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack the first "their", reading "when the hour comes". The sense is little changed. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: when the hour for them comes (B); warned you ... when they happen (R)
decisions.reason: In English "their" would point to the persecutors of verse 3, so Balanced says "the hour for them", that is, for these things (meaning decision m1). Readable says it plainly, and "warned" is what "told you" means here. Literal brackets the object English needs after "told".

decisions.choice: cuando llegue la hora en que sucedan (B); advertido ... cuando sucedan (R)
decisions.reason: "Su hora" could be heard as the persecutors' hour; the hour is the time when these things happen (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "su hora" as the Greek has it. Readable says "advertido", which is what "told you" means here.

decisions.choice: lorsque l’heure en sera venue
decisions.reason: French "leur heure", like English "their hour", would point to the persecutors of verse 3. "Their" refers to "these things" (meaning decision m1), and French says that neatly with "en": the hour of them. Literal keeps the Greek "leur heure"; Readable says "quand elles arriveront". Literal also shows the stressed "I" (m2) with "moi, je".

decisions.choice: saa yake
decisions.reason: "Their hour" is most likely the hour of "these things" (meaning note m1). Swahili "saa yake" refers back to the things, while "saa yao" would point to the persecutors of verse 3, so Swahili can keep the possessive where the English Balanced has to say "the hour for them".

source.text: Ταῦτα δὲ ὑμῖν ἐξ ἀρχῆς οὐκ εἶπον, ὅτι μεθ’ ὑμῶν ἤμην.

es.L: Y estas cosas no {{plural_you:se las|os las}} dije desde [el] principio, porque estaba con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: No {{plural_you:les|os}} dije estas cosas al principio, porque yo estaba con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: No {{plural_you:les|os}} dije estas cosas al principio, porque yo estaba aquí con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Et ces choses, je ne vous les ai pas dites dès [le] commencement, parce que j’étais avec vous.
fr.B: Je ne vous ai pas dit ces choses au début, parce que j’étais avec vous.
fr.R: Je ne vous ai pas dit ces choses au début, parce que j’étais ici avec vous.

vi.B: Lúc đầu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không nói với các con những điều này, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} còn ở với các con.
vi.R: Từ đầu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chưa nói với các con những điều này, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} còn ở đây với các con.

ko.L: 그리고 처음부터 이것들을 너희에게 말하지 않은 것은 내가 너희와 함께 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 처음에 내가 이것을 너희에게 말하지 않은 것은 내가 너희와 함께 있었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 처음에는 이런 말을 하지 않았다. 내가 여기서 너희와 함께 있었기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: from the beginning: since Jesus first called them
alternatives: the beginning of creation, as in 1:1
decisions.reason: As in 15:27, the beginning is the start of Jesus's work with his disciples (1:35-51). The phrase is close but not identical: there ἐξ is a different preposition, with the same sense.

decisions.choice: while Jesus was with them, he drew the hostility on himself and kept them; now that he is leaving, they need to be told
alternatives: Jesus had never spoken of persecution before
decisions.reason: Jesus had kept and guarded them while he was with them (17:12), and at his arrest he will ask that they be let go (18:8-9); the world's hostility fell on him. Now he is going, and they will face it without him there in person, so he tells them what is coming. Other Gospels record earlier warnings of persecution (Matthew 10:17-22); "these things" here may mean the full warning given now, with the promise of the Advocate that goes with it.

decisions.choice: here with you
decisions.reason: Readable adds "here" to show that Jesus means his bodily presence among them, now ending.

decisions.choice: aquí con ustedes
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable adds "aquí" to show that Jesus means his bodily presence among them, now ending (meaning decision m2), as at 14:25.

source.text: νῦν δὲ ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν πέμψαντά με καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐρωτᾷ με· Ποῦ ὑπάγεις;

records.literal_gloss: Now but I go to the [one] having sent me, and none of you asks me, "Where do you go?"

en.L: But now I am going to the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and none of you asks {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, 'Where are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} going?'
en.B: But now I am going to the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and not one of you asks {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, 'Where are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} going?'
en.R: But now I am going back to the Father, who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Yet not one of you is asking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, 'Where are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} going?'

es.L: Pero ahora voy al que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió, y ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pregunta: “¿Adónde vas?”.
es.B: Pero ahora me voy al que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió, y ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pregunta: “¿Adónde vas?”.
es.R: Pero ahora vuelvo al Padre, que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió. Y sin embargo, ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} está preguntando: “¿Adónde vas?”.

fr.L: Mais maintenant, je vais vers celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé, et personne d’entre vous ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} demande : “Où vas-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ?”
fr.B: Mais maintenant, je pars vers celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé, et pas un de vous ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} demande : “Où vas-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ?”
fr.R: Mais maintenant, je retourne auprès du Père, qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. Pourtant, aucun de vous ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} demande : “Où est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vas ?”

sw.L: Lakini sasa ninakwenda kwa yule aliyenituma, na hakuna hata mmoja wenu anayeniuliza, 'Unakwenda wapi?'
sw.B: Lakini sasa ninakwenda kwa yule aliyenituma, na hakuna hata mmoja wenu anayeniuliza, 'Unakwenda wapi?'
sw.R: Lakini sasa ninarudi kwa Baba, aliyenituma. Hata hivyo hakuna hata mmoja wenu anayeniuliza, 'Unakwenda wapi?'

vi.L: Nhưng bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi đến cùng Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và không ai trong các con hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: 'Thầy đi đâu?'
vi.B: Nhưng giờ đây {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi về cùng Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thế mà không ai trong các con hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: 'Thầy đi đâu?'
vi.R: Nhưng bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sắp trở về với Cha, là Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Vậy mà không ai trong các con hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: 'Thầy đi đâu vậy?'

ko.L: 그러나 이제 나는 나를 보내신 분께로 간다. 그런데 너희 가운데 아무도 나에게 '어디로 가십니까?' 하고 묻지 않는다.
ko.B: 이제 나는 나를 보내신 분께로 간다. 그런데도 너희 가운데 아무도 나에게 '어디로 가십니까?' 하고 묻지 않는다.
ko.R: 이제 나는 나를 보내신 아버지께로 돌아간다. 그런데도 너희 가운데 '어디로 가십니까?' 하고 묻는 사람이 하나도 없다.

decisions.choice: none of you asks: at this moment, none of them is asking where he goes; they think only of their own loss
alternatives: the farewell talks were joined from different occasions, and this was once spoken before 13:36 and 14:5
decisions.reason: Peter has asked "Lord, where are you going?" (13:36), and Thomas has said "we do not know where you are going" (14:5). The verb here is present: now, as Jesus speaks of going to the Father, none of them asks about it. Their earlier questions were about being left behind, and verse 6 says what fills them now: sorrow. If they asked where he is going, they would learn that he goes to the Father, which is reason for gladness (14:28). Another explanation is that the farewell talks were put together from more than one occasion. The text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: I am going to the one who sent me: Jesus's return to the Father, through his death
decisions.reason: "The one who sent me" is the Father (5:37; 7:33). Jesus came from the Father and goes back to him (13:3; 16:28). The present tense presents the going as already under way.

decisions.choice: going back to the Father, who sent me
alternatives: going to the one who sent me
decisions.reason: Readable names the Father, who in John is "the one who sent me" (meaning decision m2), and adds "back", since Jesus came from him. "Yet" shows the contrast the Greek "and" carries here.

decisions.choice: vuelvo al Padre, que me envió; sin embargo
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names the Father, who in John is "the one who sent me" (meaning decision m2), and "sin embargo" shows the contrast the Greek "and" carries here. The question keeps Peter's words of 13:36, "¿Adónde vas?".

decisions.choice: 'Thầy đi đâu?' with no setting span
decisions.reason: Where the English has the pronoun "you" under the deity_pronoun setting, Vietnamese disciples address Jesus with the noun "Thầy" (Teacher), which is always capitalised and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: '어디로 가십니까?' in the formal polite style (합쇼체)
decisions.reason: The question is put in the disciples' mouths, and disciples speak to Jesus in 합쇼체 throughout (style guide section 4).

source.text: ἀλλ’ ὅτι ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἡ λύπη πεπλήρωκεν ὑμῶν τὴν καρδίαν.

records.literal_gloss: But because these things I have spoken to you the sorrow has filled your the heart.

en.L: But because I have spoken these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart.
en.B: Instead, sorrow has filled your hearts because I have said these things to you.
en.R: Instead, you are full of sorrow, because I have told you these things.

es.L: Pero porque estas cosas {{plural_you:les|os}} he hablado, la tristeza ha llenado {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón.
es.B: Al contrario, la tristeza ha llenado {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón porque {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho estas cosas.
es.R: En cambio, {{plural_you:están|estáis}} llenos de tristeza, porque {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho estas cosas.

fr.L: Mais parce que je vous ai dit ces choses, le chagrin a rempli votre cœur.
fr.B: Au lieu de cela, le chagrin a envahi vos cœurs, parce que je vous ai dit ces choses.
fr.R: Au contraire, vous êtes pleins de chagrin, parce que je vous ai dit ces choses.

sw.L: Lakini kwa sababu nimewaambia mambo haya, huzuni imeujaza moyo wenu.
sw.B: Badala yake, huzuni imejaa mioyoni mwenu kwa sababu nimewaambia mambo haya.
sw.R: Badala yake, mmejawa na huzuni, kwa sababu nimewaambia mambo haya.

vi.L: Nhưng vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói những điều này với các con, nỗi buồn đã tràn đầy lòng các con.
vi.B: Trái lại, nỗi buồn đã tràn ngập lòng các con vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con những điều này.
vi.R: Trái lại, lòng các con đầy buồn rầu, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con những điều này.

ko.L: 오히려 내가 이것들을 너희에게 말하였기 때문에 슬픔이 너희 마음을 가득 채웠다.
ko.B: 도리어 내가 이런 말을 했기 때문에 너희 마음에 슬픔이 가득하다.
ko.R: 오히려 내가 이 말을 하니까 너희는 슬픔에 잠겨 있다.

decisions.choice: sorrow: grief and distress, here at the thought of losing Jesus
decisions.reason: The noun λύπη is grief or pain of heart. It recurs in 16:20-22, where Jesus says their sorrow will be turned into joy, like a woman's pain in childbirth. Here it is the grief of friends about to be left.

decisions.choice: but: instead of asking, they grieve; your heart: each one's heart
decisions.reason: The "but" sets their sorrow against the question they do not ask (verse 5). "Your" is plural and "heart" singular, as in 14:1 and 14:27: each of them inwardly. The perfect tense "has filled" describes their state now.

decisions.choice: Instead (B, R); your hearts (B); you are full of sorrow (R)
decisions.reason: "Instead" shows what the "but" contrasts (meaning decision m2). Balanced makes "hearts" plural, the natural way to speak of many people's hearts, as at 14:27. Readable puts the result first in plain words.

decisions.choice: Al contrario (B); En cambio (R); su corazón, singular (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Al contrario" and "en cambio" show what the "but" contrasts (meaning decision m2). Spanish says "su corazón" naturally of many people, as at 14:1 and 14:27, so Balanced keeps the Greek singular.

decisions.choice: le chagrin
decisions.reason: The noun is grief at the thought of losing Jesus (meaning decision m1). "Chagrin" is the everyday French word for the grief of losing someone dear and is plain enough for every level. The same noun returns in 16:20-22, which should use the same French; a reviewer should check it, since that passage was drafted separately.

source.text: ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ τὴν ἀλήθειαν λέγω ὑμῖν, συμφέρει ὑμῖν ἵνα ἐγὼ ἀπέλθω.

records.literal_gloss: But I the truth say to you, it is profitable for you that I go away.

en.L: But I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away.
en.B: But I am telling you the truth: my going away is to your advantage.
en.R: But this is the truth: it is better for you that I am going away.

es.L: Pero yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo la verdad: {{plural_you:les|os}} conviene que yo me vaya.
es.B: Sin embargo, yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo la verdad: {{plural_you:les|os}} conviene que me vaya.
es.R: Pero esta es la verdad: es mejor para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que yo me vaya.

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je vous dis la vérité : il vous est utile que je m’en aille.
fr.B: Pourtant, je vous dis la vérité : {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} départ est dans votre intérêt.
fr.R: Mais voici la vérité : c’est mieux pour vous que je parte.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nawaambia kweli: ni faida kwenu {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niondoke.
sw.B: Lakini ninawaambia kweli: kuondoka {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} ni faida kwenu.
sw.R: Lakini huu ndio ukweli: ni afadhali kwenu kwamba ninaondoka.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con sự thật: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ra đi thì có ích cho các con.
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói thật với các con: việc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ra đi là có lợi cho các con.
vi.R: Nhưng đây là sự thật: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ra đi thì tốt hơn cho các con.

ko.L: 그러나 나는 너희에게 진실을 말한다. 내가 떠나가는 것이 너희에게 유익하다.
ko.B: 그러나 내가 너희에게 진실을 말한다. 내가 떠나가는 것이 너희에게 유익하다.
ko.R: 그러나 이것은 사실이다. 내가 떠나가는 것이 너희에게 더 좋다.

decisions.choice: it is to your advantage: it is for your good, it works to your benefit
decisions.reason: The verb συμφέρει means to be useful or profitable. Jesus's going away seems the worst thing that could happen to them; he says it is for their good, and verse 7b gives the reason.

decisions.choice: the same words as Caiaphas: "it is to your advantage that"
decisions.reason: Caiaphas said to the council that it was to their advantage that one man should die for the people (11:50; recalled in 18:14), using the same verb with "to you" and "that". John has said that Caiaphas spoke more truly than he knew (11:51-52). Here Jesus himself says that his departure, which comes through that death, is to his disciples' advantage.

decisions.choice: I tell you the truth: an emphatic assurance against what they feel
decisions.reason: The "I" is emphatic, and the truth is put first: whatever their sorrow tells them, this is the truth. Truth is a key term.

decisions.choice: it is to your advantage (L); my going away is to your advantage (B); it is better for you (R)
decisions.reason: Each level uses the wording it used for Caiaphas's words at 11:50, so readers can hear the echo (meaning decision m2). Balanced makes "my going away" the subject, which keeps the stress on the going.

decisions.choice: les conviene (L, B); es mejor para ustedes (R)
decisions.reason: Each level uses the wording it used for Caiaphas's words at 11:50, so readers can hear the echo (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: il vous est utile (L); est dans votre intérêt (B); c’est mieux pour vous (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means "be useful, be to someone's good" (meaning decision m1). These are the same words Caiaphas used in 11:50 (m2), so each level should match the French used there; a reviewer should compare the two, since 11:50 was drafted separately. Literal shows the stressed "I" (m3) with "moi, je", and Balanced's "mon départ" takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: ni faida kwenu (L, B); ni afadhali kwenu (R)
decisions.reason: Each level uses the words it used for Caiaphas at 11:50, so the echo can be heard (meaning note m2). Readable says "ukweli", the everyday noun, in "huu ndio ukweli"; Literal and Balanced keep the key term "kweli".

decisions.choice: sự thật / nói thật
decisions.reason: Here "the truth" is a plain assurance that what he says is so, not the key term "truth" as God's revealed reality; the style guide keeps "chân lý" for the key term and "sự thật" for a plain fact.

decisions.choice: 진실 (L, B); 사실 (R) for "the truth" here
decisions.reason: Here "the truth" is an assurance that what Jesus says is so, not the key term for God's truth; 진리 would sound like a teaching about truth. 진리 stays for the key term (verse 13).

source.text: ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ ἀπέλθω, ὁ παράκλητος οὐ μὴ ἔλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς· ἐὰν δὲ πορευθῶ, πέμψω αὐτὸν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: If for not I go away, the advocate not not will come to you; if but I go, I will send him to you.

en.L: For if I do not go away, the Advocate will certainly not come to you; but if I go, I will send {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to you.
en.B: For if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you at all; but if I go, I will send {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to you.
en.R: If I do not leave, the Advocate will never come to you. But if I do go, I will send {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to you.

es.L: Porque si no me voy, el Defensor no vendrá de ningún modo a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; pero si parto, {{plural_you:se|os}} {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} enviaré.
es.B: Porque si no me voy, el Defensor no vendrá en absoluto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; pero si me voy, {{plural_you:se|os}} {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} enviaré.
es.R: Si no me voy, el Defensor nunca vendrá a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Pero si me voy, yo {{plural_you:se|os}} {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} enviaré.

fr.L: Car si je ne m’en vais pas, le Défenseur ne viendra certainement pas vers vous ; mais si je pars, je vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}enverrai.
fr.B: Car si je ne m’en vais pas, le Défenseur ne viendra pas du tout vers vous ; mais si je pars, je vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}enverrai.
fr.R: Si je ne pars pas, le Défenseur ne viendra jamais vers vous. Mais si je pars, je vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}enverrai.

sw.L: Kwa maana nisipoondoka, yule Mtetezi hatakuja kwenu kamwe; lakini nikienda, nitamtuma kwenu.
sw.B: Kwa maana nisipoondoka, Mtetezi hatakuja kwenu hata kidogo; lakini nikienda, nitamtuma kwenu.
sw.R: Nisipoondoka, Mtetezi hatakuja kwenu kamwe. Lakini nikienda, nitamtuma kwenu.

vi.L: Vì nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không ra đi, Đấng Biện Hộ chắc chắn sẽ không đến với các con; nhưng nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sai {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến với các con.
vi.B: Vì nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không ra đi, Đấng Biện Hộ sẽ không đến với các con đâu; còn nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sai {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến với các con.
vi.R: Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không đi, Đấng Biện Hộ sẽ không bao giờ đến với các con. Nhưng nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sai {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến với các con.

ko.L: 만일 내가 떠나가지 않으면 변호자께서 결코 너희에게 오시지 않을 것이기 때문이다. 그러나 내가 가면, 내가 그분을 너희에게 보낼 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 떠나가지 않으면 변호자께서 너희에게 오시지 않는다. 그러나 내가 가면 그분을 너희에게 보내겠다.
ko.R: 내가 떠나지 않으면 변호자께서 절대로 너희에게 오시지 않는다. 그러나 내가 가면 그분을 너희에게 보내 주겠다.

decisions.choice: the Advocate: one called to stand beside another and speak for them
decisions.reason: The word παράκλητος was used of someone called to stand by a person, above all in a court. It is the same title as in 14:16, 14:26 and 15:26, the Holy Spirit. The next verses show him in a court setting: he will prove the world wrong (verses 8-11).

decisions.choice: the Spirit is given when Jesus has gone to the Father
decisions.reason: John has already said that the Spirit had not yet been given because Jesus had not yet been glorified (7:39). Jesus must go by way of the cross to the Father before he sends the Advocate. The risen Jesus breathes on his disciples and says "Receive the Holy Spirit" (20:22).

decisions.choice: will certainly not come: a strong double negative; I will send him: Jesus himself sends the Advocate
decisions.reason: The two negatives οὐ μὴ together make the strongest denial Greek has. In 14:16, 26 the Father gives and sends the Advocate; here and in 15:26 Jesus sends him. The two verbs for going, ἀπέλθω and πορευθῶ, mean the same here. The masculine pronoun αὐτὸν agrees with the masculine word for Advocate.

decisions.choice: the Advocate
decisions.reason: The book uses "the Advocate" at every level, because John's setting is testimony and judgment (meaning decision m1). Other well-known renderings are Helper, Counselor and Comforter; each catches part of the sense.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: The Spirit is never "it" in this translation. "Him" takes the deity pronoun setting like every pronoun for God. Literal shows the double negative with "certainly", Balanced with "at all" and Readable with "never" (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: el Defensor
decisions.reason: As at 14:16, 14:26 and 15:26: one called to stand beside someone and speak for them (meaning decision m1). The Spirit is referred to by "lo", which takes the deity_pronoun setting by the book-wide rule (1:1), with the plural_you span split around it. The double negative is "de ningún modo" (L), "en absoluto" (B) and "nunca" (R) (meaning decision m3); Literal shows the two Greek verbs for going with "me voy" and "parto".

decisions.choice: le Défenseur; je vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}enverrai
decisions.reason: The book-wide French word for this title, as in 14:16, where the choice and the other renderings are explained; the court setting of verses 8-11 suits it well (meaning decision m1). The object pronoun for the Spirit takes the deity_pronoun setting in its elided form. Literal shows the double negative with "certainement", Balanced with "pas du tout" and Readable with "jamais" (m3).

decisions.choice: Mtetezi; hatakuja ... kamwe (L, R), hata kidogo (B)
decisions.reason: "Mtetezi" (Advocate), as at 14:16, 14:26 and 15:26. "Kamwe" and "hata kidogo" carry the strong double negative (meaning note m3). "Him" is the object marker in "nitamtuma", so Swahili has no span where the English has one.

decisions.choice: Đấng Biện Hộ
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for the whole book: the context of 16:8-11 is testimony and judgment, so the word for one who speaks for another in court. Other translations say "Đấng Yên Ủi" (Comforter) or "Đấng Trợ Giúp" (Helper).

decisions.choice: 변호자 for paraklētos at every level
decisions.reason: The context is testimony and judgment (16:8-11), so the guide uses 변호자, "one who speaks for another"; 보혜사 is the familiar church word, and 위로자 and 돕는 분 are other readings of the title.

decisions.choice: The Advocate takes the honorific (변호자께서 오시다) and is referred to as 그분
decisions.reason: The Spirit is spoken of as a person and as God, so Korean gives him 께서, -시- and 그분 in place of the English deity_pronoun spans (style guide section 7).

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 오시면, 죄에 대하여 그리고 의에 대하여 그리고 심판에 대하여 세상의 잘못을 밝혀 드러내실 것이다.
ko.B: 그분이 오시면 죄와 의와 심판에 대하여 세상이 잘못되었음을 밝히실 것이다.
ko.R: 그분이 오시면, 세상이 죄와 의와 심판에 대해 틀렸다는 것을 보여 주실 것이다.

decisions.choice: convict: expose and prove wrong, as a case is proved in court
alternatives: convince, bring to inner conviction and repentance
decisions.reason: The verb ἐλέγξει means to bring something into the open and prove it, to show someone in the wrong. In 3:20 evil deeds are exposed by the light; in 8:46 Jesus asks who can prove him guilty of sin. The setting here is a trial: the world has judged Jesus, and the Advocate reopens the case and shows the world to be wrong. The word does not say whether the world will accept the verdict. Some will be convinced and believe; others will stand condemned. The Spirit does this through the disciples' testimony (15:26-27).

decisions.choice: the world: humanity organized against God
decisions.reason: As in 15:18-19, the world is people as they set themselves against God and his messenger. It has hated Jesus (15:18) and will hate his disciples.

decisions.choice: three heads of the charge, each explained in the verses that follow
decisions.reason: Sin, righteousness and judgment are three points on which the world is shown to be in the wrong; verses 9, 10 and 11 each give a reason with "because". Righteousness is a key term. The masculine ἐκεῖνος ("that one", "he") agrees with the Advocate of verse 7.

decisions.choice: show the world to be in the wrong (B); show the world that it is wrong (R)
decisions.reason: "Convict" in English now suggests a verdict of guilty in court, which fits sin but not righteousness. Balanced and Readable say what the verb does in all three cases: it proves the world wrong (meaning decision m1). The footnote gives "convict".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: The Advocate is never "it". "He" takes the deity pronoun setting. Literal says "he" for the emphatic "that one", as at 14:26 and 15:26.

decisions.choice: pondrá al descubierto (L); demostrará que ... está equivocado (B); le mostrará ... que está equivocado (R)
decisions.reason: The verb exposes and proves wrong, as a case is proved in court (meaning decision m1). "Convencer de" now suggests persuading someone, and "redargüir" is a word few readers know. The stressed "él" for "that one" takes the deity pronoun setting, as at 15:26. The footnote gives "convencerá".

decisions.choice: confondra (L); montrera que le monde est dans l’erreur (B); montrera au monde qu’il se trompe (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to expose and prove someone wrong, as in court (meaning decision m1). "Convaincre" had that sense in older French but now means "persuade", and "accuser" fits sin but not righteousness. "Confondre" means to prove someone wrong publicly; Balanced and Readable say what it does in all three cases. In "qu’il se trompe" the "il" is the world and has no setting.

decisions.choice: la justice
decisions.reason: French "justice" covers both justice and righteousness and is the usual word for this key term in French Bibles; "droiture" would narrow it to personal uprightness. Verse 10 shows what it means here (meaning decision m1 there).

decisions.choice: atauthibitishia ulimwengu [kosa lake] (L); atauonyesha ulimwengu kwamba umekosea (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to expose and prove someone wrong, as in a court (meaning note m1). Literal uses "kuthibitishia", the verb of 8:46 ("who proves me guilty of sin"), and brackets the object Swahili needs. Balanced and Readable say what the verb does in all three cases: it shows the world to be wrong. "Haki" is the key term for righteousness.

decisions.choice: Đấng ấy sẽ vạch trần (L); sẽ chỉ ra rằng thế gian đã sai lầm (B); cho thế gian thấy họ sai (R)
decisions.reason: "Vạch trần" (expose) keeps the courtroom sense of proving someone wrong; "buộc tội" (accuse) would say less than prove. Literal renders "that one" as "Đấng ấy", the respectful demonstrative for the Advocate.

decisions.choice: 잘못을 밝혀 드러내다 (L); 잘못되었음을 밝히다 (B); 틀렸다는 것을 보여 주다 (R) for "convict"
decisions.reason: The verb means to expose and prove wrong, as in a court; 책망하다 (rebuke) and 깨닫게 하다 (make aware) each give only part of it.

decisions.choice: Korean puts the three heads of the charge before the verb
alternatives: the verb first, as in the Greek
decisions.reason: Korean is verb-final; the list 죄에 대하여 ... 심판에 대하여 comes before 밝혀 드러내실 것이다, and verses 9-11 take up each head in turn.

decisions.choice: about sin: the world is wrong about what sin is and guilty of it, for its sin is not believing in Jesus
alternatives: the Spirit convicts people of their sins in general, and unbelief is the evidence
the world sins in that it does not believe
decisions.reason: In John the sin above all others is refusing to believe in the one God sent: "unless you believe that I am, you will die in your sins" (8:24; compare 3:18-19; 9:41; 15:22, 24). The world thought Jesus was the sinner (9:24). The Spirit shows that the guilt lies with those who will not believe in him. The word ὅτι can mean "because" or "in that"; either way unbelief is the heart of the world's sin.

decisions.choice: they: the people of the world
decisions.reason: The plural verb takes "the world" of verse 8 as the people in it.

decisions.choice: about sin ... ; about righteousness ... ; about judgment ... (verses 9-11 continue one sentence)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps verses 8 to 11 as one English sentence, with each verse taking up one of the three points, as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: It is wrong about sin; people
decisions.reason: Readable makes each of verses 9 to 11 a sentence, repeating "it is wrong about" from verse 8, and says "people" for the plural "they" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Está equivocado acerca de; la gente
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable makes each of verses 9 to 11 a sentence, repeating "está equivocado" from verse 8, and says "la gente" for the plural "they" (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep verses 8 to 11 as one sentence.

decisions.choice: about righteousness: the world was wrong about who is righteous; Jesus's going to the Father shows that God has vindicated him
alternatives: the world's own righteousness is shown to be false
the righteousness God gives is made available through Jesus's going
decisions.reason: The world judged Jesus a sinner and put him to death as one (9:24; 18:30; 19:7). His going to the Father, through death and resurrection, is God's verdict that he was in the right; he goes to the one who sent him, which no sinner could do. The world's own claim to righteousness is shown up by the same verdict. John uses the word δικαιοσύνης only here and in verse 8, so its sense must be taken from this context. Righteousness is a key term.

decisions.choice: you no longer see me: the disciples, addressed directly; Jesus will no longer be with them as before
decisions.reason: The verse moves from "they" (the world) to "you" (the disciples). Jesus's going means that even they will not see him as they do now; the righteousness that is his is now hidden with the Father, and the Advocate makes it known. Yet in verse 16 he adds that in a little while they will see him again. The present θεωρεῖτέ is used of what is about to be true.

decisions.choice: you will see me no longer (B); you will not see me anymore (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the future for the present tense that looks to what is about to happen (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: ya no me verán
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable use the future for the present tense that looks to what is about to happen (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: about judgment: the world judged Jesus, but in truth its ruler is the one judged
alternatives: the world will face God's judgment at the end
the Spirit shows what true judgment is
decisions.reason: The world condemned Jesus, and so passed judgment wrongly (7:24; 8:15). At the cross the verdict is turned around: "now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out" (12:31). The ruler who seemed to win at the cross has been condemned there. So the world's judgment is shown to be false, and the world under that ruler stands judged with him.

decisions.choice: the ruler of this world: Satan
decisions.reason: The same title as in 12:31 and 14:30. He is the devil, who put the betrayal into Judas's heart (13:2, 27).

decisions.choice: has been judged: a perfect tense; the verdict is already given, though the cross is still ahead
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks from the point of view of the Advocate's coming, when the cross is past, and of his own certainty that the hour has come (12:31, "now"). The perfect κέκριται means the verdict is given and stands.

decisions.choice: and about judgment
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "and" before the last of the three points, as English lists do; Literal has it too, where the Greek has a joining "but". Balanced says "stands judged" for the perfect tense: the verdict is given and remains (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Satan, the ruler of this world; already
decisions.reason: As at 12:31 and 14:30, Readable names Satan, whom the title means (meaning decision m2); Jesus is the speaker, and he knows who the ruler is. Every level keeps "the ruler of this world" as at 12:31. "Already" brings out the perfect tense (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: el gobernante de este mundo (L, B); Satanás, el que gobierna este mundo (R); ya está juzgado (B); ya ha sido juzgado (R)
decisions.reason: Each level uses its wording of 12:31 and 14:30 (meaning decision m2). "Ya" brings out the perfect tense: the verdict is given and stands (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: le prince de ce monde (L, B); Satan, celui qui domine ce monde (R); a été jugé (L); est jugé (B)
decisions.reason: The title as in 14:30 and 12:31 (meaning decision m2), with Readable naming Satan as there. The perfect tense means the verdict is given and stands (m3): Balanced says "est jugé", a French present passive that describes the settled state, as the English says "stands judged".

decisions.choice: mtawala wa ulimwengu huu; Shetani added at Readable
decisions.reason: As at 12:31 and 14:30. Balanced says "amekwisha kuhukumiwa" for the perfect tense, the verdict already given (meaning note m3).

decisions.choice: Sa-tan; kẻ cai trị
decisions.reason: "Sa-tan" is the established Protestant spelling. "Kẻ" rather than "người" for the ruler of this world, since Vietnamese marks a hostile figure with "kẻ".

decisions.choice: 통치자 for "ruler"
decisions.reason: 통치자 is the plain modern word for one who rules; 임금 (king) is the older church rendering and narrows the sense.

decisions.choice: 이미 ("already") at Balanced
decisions.reason: The Greek perfect means the verdict stands now; Korean shows that with 이미, as the English "stands judged" does.

source.text: Ἔτι πολλὰ ἔχω ὑμῖν λέγειν, ἀλλ’ οὐ δύνασθε βαστάζειν ἄρτι·

records.literal_gloss: Still many things I have to you to say, but not you are able to bear now;

en.L: I have many things still to say to you, but you are not able to bear [them] now.
en.B: There is much more I have to tell you, but it is more than you can bear right now.
en.R: I have much more to tell you, but right now it would be too much for you.

es.L: Aún tengo muchas cosas que {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}}, pero no [las] {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} cargar ahora.
es.B: Tengo mucho más que {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}}, pero ahora mismo sería una carga demasiado pesada para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Tengo mucho más que {{plural_you:decirles|deciros}}, pero por ahora sería demasiado para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: J’ai encore bien des choses à vous dire, mais vous ne pouvez pas [les] porter à présent.
fr.B: J’ai encore beaucoup à vous dire, mais pour l’instant ce serait un fardeau trop lourd pour vous.
fr.R: J’ai encore beaucoup de choses à vous dire, mais en ce moment, ce serait trop pour vous.

sw.L: Bado nina mambo mengi ya kuwaambia, lakini hamwezi kuyabeba sasa.
sw.B: Ningali na mengi ya kuwaambia, lakini sasa hivi ni mazito mno kwenu.
sw.R: Nina mengi zaidi ya kuwaambia, lakini sasa hivi yangekuwa mengi mno kwenu.

vi.L: Ta còn nhiều điều để nói với các con, nhưng bây giờ các con không thể mang nổi [chúng].
vi.B: Ta còn nhiều điều nữa phải nói với các con, nhưng bây giờ các con chưa thể gánh nổi.
vi.R: Ta còn nhiều điều muốn nói với các con, nhưng lúc này các con chưa chịu nổi đâu.

ko.L: 아직도 내가 너희에게 말할 것이 많지만, 지금은 너희가 [그것들을] 감당할 수 없다.
ko.B: 내가 너희에게 할 말이 아직 많지만, 지금은 너희가 그것을 다 감당하지 못한다.
ko.R: 너희에게 해 줄 말이 아직 많다. 그러나 지금은 너희가 그것을 다 받아들이기 힘들다.

decisions.choice: bear: carry a load; here, take in and endure what he would say
decisions.reason: The verb βαστάζειν means to carry something heavy (19:17, of Jesus carrying his cross). What Jesus still has to say would be too heavy for them now, in their sorrow and before his death and resurrection. Only after he was raised did they understand what he had said and done (2:22; 12:16).

decisions.choice: many things still to say: what the Spirit will make known (verses 13-15)
alternatives: new teaching beyond what Jesus taught
decisions.reason: Verses 13-15 say how these things will be told: the Spirit will take what is Jesus's and declare it. So the "many things" are not a different message, but a fuller understanding of Jesus and what is to come (14:26).

decisions.choice: more than you can bear right now (B); it would be too much for you (R)
alternatives: you are not able to bear [them] now (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the weight the subject, which is how English says this. "Right now" carries the stress the Greek puts on "now": it will not always be so.

decisions.choice: cargar (L); una carga demasiado pesada (B); sería demasiado (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is carrying a load, as of the cross at 19:17 (meaning decision m1), so Literal and Balanced keep the picture. "Ahora mismo" and "por ahora" carry the stress the Greek puts on "now": it will not always be so.

decisions.choice: porter à présent (L); un fardeau trop lourd pour l’instant (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to carry a heavy load (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "porter" and uses "à présent" for the sharp word for "now", as in 13:37; Balanced keeps the picture with "fardeau". French needs an object, which Literal brackets.

source.text: ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ ἐκεῖνος, τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας, ὁδηγήσει ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ πάσῃ, οὐ γὰρ λαλήσει ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ, ἀλλ’ ὅσα ἀκούσει λαλήσει, καὶ τὰ ἐρχόμενα ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: When but comes that one, the Spirit of the truth, he will guide you in the truth all; not for he will speak from himself, but as much as he will hear he will speak, and the things coming he will declare to you.

en.L: But when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes, the Spirit of truth, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will guide you in all the truth; for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not speak from {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, but whatever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hears {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will speak, and the things that are coming {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will declare to you.
en.B: But when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, the Spirit of truth, comes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will guide you in all the truth. What {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says will not come from {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will speak what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hears, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make known to you what is yet to come.
en.R: But the Spirit of truth will come, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will guide you in all the truth. His words will not come from {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. He will say only what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hears, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will tell you about the things that are still to come.

es.L: Pero cuando venga {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, el Espíritu de la verdad, {{plural_you:los|os}} guiará en toda la verdad; porque no hablará por {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo, sino que hablará todo lo que oiga, y {{plural_you:les|os}} anunciará las cosas que vienen.
es.B: Pero cuando venga {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, el Espíritu de la verdad, {{plural_you:los|os}} guiará en toda la verdad. Lo que diga no saldrá de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo: dirá lo que oiga, y {{plural_you:les|os}} dará a conocer lo que está por venir.
es.R: Pero el Espíritu de la verdad vendrá, y cuando venga, {{plural_you:los|os}} guiará en toda la verdad. Sus palabras no saldrán de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo. Dirá solo lo que oiga, y {{plural_you:les|os}} hablará de las cosas que todavía han de venir.

fr.L: Mais quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} viendra, l’Esprit de la vérité, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous guidera dans toute la vérité ; car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne parlera pas de {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, mais tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entendra, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le dira, et les choses qui viennent, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous les annoncera.
fr.B: Mais quand viendra l’Esprit de vérité, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous guidera dans toute la vérité. Ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dira ne viendra pas de {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dira ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entendra, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous fera connaître ce qui doit venir.
fr.R: Mais l’Esprit de vérité viendra, et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sera là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous guidera dans toute la vérité. Ses paroles ne viendront pas de {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}. Il dira seulement ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entend, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous parlera des choses qui doivent encore arriver.

sw.L: Lakini atakapokuja huyo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, Roho wa kweli, atawaongoza katika kweli yote; kwa maana hatasema kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, bali yote atakayoyasikia atayasema, na mambo yajayo atawatangazia.
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, Roho wa kweli, atakapokuja, atawaongoza katika kweli yote. Atakayoyasema hayatatoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}; atasema yale anayoyasikia, na atawajulisha mambo yatakayokuja.
sw.R: Lakini Roho wa kweli atakuja, na atakapokuja, atawaongoza katika kweli yote. Maneno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} hayatatoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}. Atasema tu yale anayoyasikia, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atawaeleza mambo ambayo bado yatakuja.

vi.L: Nhưng khi Đấng ấy đến, là Thánh Linh của chân lý, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ dẫn dắt các con trong mọi chân lý; vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ không nói từ chính mình, nhưng điều gì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghe, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ nói, và những việc sắp đến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ báo cho các con.
vi.B: Nhưng khi Thánh Linh của chân lý đến, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ dẫn dắt các con trong mọi chân lý. Những gì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói sẽ không tự {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà ra; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ nói những gì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghe, và sẽ cho các con biết những việc sắp xảy đến.
vi.R: Nhưng Thánh Linh của chân lý sẽ đến, và khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ dẫn dắt các con trong tất cả chân lý. Lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói không phải tự {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà ra. Ngài chỉ nói những gì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghe, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ cho các con biết những việc sắp xảy ra.

ko.L: 그러나 그분, 곧 진리의 영께서 오시면, 그분이 너희를 모든 진리 안에서 인도하실 것이다. 그분은 스스로 말씀하지 않으시고, 무엇이든지 들으시는 것을 말씀하실 것이며, 오고 있는 일들을 너희에게 알려 주실 것이기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러나 진리의 영이신 그분이 오시면, 너희를 모든 진리 안에서 인도하실 것이다. 그분은 자기 생각대로 말씀하지 않으시고 들으시는 것을 말씀하시며, 앞으로 올 일을 너희에게 알려 주실 것이다.
ko.R: 그러나 진리의 영께서 오실 것이다. 그분이 오시면 너희를 이끄셔서 모든 진리를 알게 하실 것이다. 그분은 스스로 말씀하지 않으신다. 들으신 것만 말씀하시고, 앞으로 일어날 일들을 너희에게 알려 주실 것이다.

decisions.choice: "that one", masculine, then "the Spirit", neuter, in apposition: the Advocate spoken of as a person
alternatives: the neuter means the Spirit is an impersonal force
the masculine is a deliberate statement that the Spirit is a person
decisions.reason: The pronoun ἐκεῖνος is masculine, carrying on the Advocate of verses 7-8, and then "the Spirit of truth" is added, a neuter noun, to say who he is. Grammar explains the masculine, so it does not prove a point on its own, and the neuter noun says nothing about whether the Spirit is a thing (as in 14:17, 26). What shows him as a person is what he does here: he guides, hears, speaks, declares and glorifies.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of truth: the Holy Spirit, who comes from the God of truth and makes the truth known
alternatives: a spirit or attitude of truthfulness
decisions.reason: This is the Advocate already named "the Spirit of truth" (14:17; 15:26) and "the Holy Spirit" (14:26). He leads into the truth that Jesus is (14:6). Truth is a key term.

decisions.choice: in all the truth (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "into all the truth", with a different preposition and word order; important early manuscripts have "in all the truth", as the SBLGNT does. The difference is slight: "in" pictures guidance within the whole of the truth, "into" a leading toward it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: he will not speak from himself: the Spirit's message comes from the Father and the Son
decisions.reason: Jesus says the same of himself: he does not speak on his own, but what the Father has taught him (7:16-18; 8:28; 12:49; 14:10). The Spirit likewise speaks what he hears; verses 14-15 say that what he hears and takes is Jesus's, and all that is Jesus's is the Father's. The SBLGNT has the future "will hear"; some manuscripts have the present "hears", with the same sense.

decisions.choice: the things that are coming: what was still ahead for the disciples, beginning with Jesus's death and resurrection and the life of the church that followed
alternatives: only events at the end of the age
decisions.reason: The phrase is open. From where the disciples stand the coming things begin with the hour now at hand; the Spirit will show them what these mean, and what is to follow. The verb ἀναγγελεῖ ("declare, announce") was used by the Samaritan woman of the Messiah: "he will declare all things to us" (4:25). Here it is the Spirit who declares.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} for the Spirit
decisions.reason: The Spirit is never "it" in this translation. The Greek pronoun and verbs agree with the Advocate, a masculine noun, and the Spirit is a person (meaning decision m1), so every level says "he" and "himself", with the deity pronoun setting as for the Father and the Son. A sentence that starts with "He" or "His" has the capital either way and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: when he, the Spirit of truth, comes (B); the Spirit of truth will come, and when he does (R); what he says will not come from himself (B); his words will not come from himself (R)
alternatives: when he comes, the Spirit of truth (Literal)
he will not speak from himself (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the name next to the pronoun it explains; Readable uses the name alone. "From himself" means "on his own": Balanced and Readable say that his words do not start with him (meaning decision m4). Readable adds "only", which the contrast with "not from himself" implies.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} for the Spirit
decisions.reason: The Spirit is a person (meaning decision m1). Spanish "Espíritu" is masculine, so the pronouns are personal with no change. Every pronoun for the Spirit takes the deity pronoun setting by the book-wide rule (1:1), except "Sus" where it opens a sentence (Readable). Literal says "anunciará", the verb of 4:25 (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: en toda la verdad
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "in all the truth" (meaning decision m3); "a toda la verdad" would follow the other reading, "into".

decisions.choice: dans toute la vérité
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "in all the truth" (meaning decision m3), guidance within the whole of the truth, and French "dans" says that; "vers" would follow the other reading. As in 14:16-17, French "il" and "lui-même" agree with "Esprit" and "Défenseur" and say that the Spirit is a person; they take the deity_pronoun setting, with a plain capital at the start of a sentence ("Il dira", "Ses paroles").

decisions.choice: personal agreement for Roho (atakapokuja, atawaongoza); huyo yeye (L) for the emphatic "that one"
alternatives: agreement with roho as a thing
decisions.reason: As at 14:16-17 and 14:26: Roho takes personal agreement, and the free pronouns for him (yeye, naye, yake, kwake mwenyewe) carry the reader setting (meaning note m1). Literal says "huyo yeye" for the emphatic pronoun, as at 14:26. "Katika kweli yote" follows the SBLGNT "in" (m3).

decisions.choice: Thánh Linh của chân lý
decisions.reason: The guide's "Thánh Linh" for the Spirit with the key term "chân lý" for truth. "Thần lẽ thật" is the 1926 wording and archaic; "thần" alone can suggest a lesser spirit or god.

decisions.choice: nói từ chính mình
decisions.reason: The reflexive "mình" carries "himself" without a pronoun, so Literal needs no setting span here; Balanced and Readable use "tự Ngài" with the setting.

decisions.choice: 진리의 영 for "the Spirit of truth"
decisions.reason: 영 with the genitive keeps the Greek title; 진리 is the key term for truth, kept at every level.

decisions.choice: The "for" clause is rendered with -기 때문이다 at the end of the sentence
decisions.reason: Korean gives the reason at the end of the clause chain; Balanced and Readable leave the link implied.

source.text: ἐκεῖνος ἐμὲ δοξάσει, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ ἐμοῦ λήμψεται καὶ ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: That one me will glorify, because from the mine he will take and will declare to you.

en.L: He will glorify {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will take from what is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} and will declare [it] to you.
en.B: He will glorify {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will receive from what is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} and make it known to you.
en.R: He will bring glory to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. He will take what belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and tell it to you.

es.L: Él {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glorificará a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, porque tomará de lo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}} y [lo] anunciará a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Él {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glorificará, porque recibirá de lo que es {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}} y {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} dará a conocer.
es.R: Él mostrará {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} gloria. Tomará lo que es {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}} y {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} contará.

fr.L: Lui, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glorifiera, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prendra de ce qui est à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et vous [l’]annoncera.
fr.B: C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glorifiera, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} recevra de ce qui est à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et vous le fera connaître.
fr.R: Il {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glorifiera. Il prendra ce qui est à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous le fera connaître.

sw.L: Huyo atanitukuza {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, kwa sababu atachukua katika yaliyo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kuwatangazia.
sw.B: Yeye atanitukuza {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, kwa sababu atapokea katika yaliyo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kuwajulisha.
sw.R: Yeye atanitukuza. Atachukua yaliyo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kuwaeleza.

vi.L: Đấng ấy sẽ tôn vinh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ lấy từ những gì thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và sẽ báo [điều đó] cho các con.
vi.B: Ngài sẽ tôn vinh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ nhận từ những gì thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà cho các con biết.
vi.R: Ngài sẽ đem vinh quang đến cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ngài sẽ lấy những gì thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà nói lại cho các con.

ko.L: 그분이 나를 영광스럽게 하실 것이다. 그분이 내 것에서 받아 너희에게 알려 주실 것이기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그분은 나를 영광스럽게 하실 것이다. 내 것을 받아서 너희에게 알려 주실 것이기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그분은 나를 영광스럽게 하실 것이다. 나에게 있는 것을 가져다가 너희에게 알려 주실 것이다.

decisions.choice: he will glorify me: the Spirit makes Jesus known for who he is
decisions.reason: To glorify is to show someone's true worth and greatness. The Spirit does not draw attention to himself; he makes known Jesus, who is glorified in his death, resurrection and return to the Father (12:23; 13:31-32; 17:1, 5). The "me" stands first for emphasis. Glorify is a key term.

decisions.choice: take from what is mine: draw on what belongs to Jesus, his words, his work and all that he is
decisions.reason: The Greek has "from the mine", meaning from what is Jesus's own. Verse 15 explains how much that is: all that the Father has.

decisions.choice: He (plain at sentence start); {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will take; {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}
decisions.reason: The Spirit is "he", never "it". The sentence opens with plain "He", which is capitalised either way; the later "he" carries the deity pronoun setting like every pronoun for God. "Me" and "mine" are Jesus speaking of himself and take the setting too.

decisions.choice: receive ... make it known (B); bring glory to; take what belongs to me and tell it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "receive", since the Spirit takes what is given him, and "make known" for the verb "declare". Readable says "bring glory to", keeping the key word glory, and uses everyday words for the rest.

decisions.choice: me glorificará a mí (L); me glorificará (B); mostrará mi gloria (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "me" first for emphasis (meaning decision m1); Literal shows it with the doubled "a mí". Readable says "mostrar la gloria", as at 12:28 and 14:13. "Él" at the start of a sentence is written plain; "me", "mi" and "mío" for Jesus take the deity pronoun setting by the book-wide rule (1:1).

decisions.choice: Lui, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} (L); C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek begins with the emphatic "that one" (meaning decision m1). Literal gives it with "Lui, il", the first word plain because it opens the sentence; Balanced with "c’est lui qui". Readable keeps "glorifier", the key term, rather than the English Readable's "bring glory to", since the French verb is common.

source.text: πάντα ὅσα ἔχει ὁ πατὴρ ἐμά ἐστιν· διὰ τοῦτο εἶπον ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ ἐμοῦ λαμβάνει καὶ ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: All things as many as has the Father mine are; because of this I said that from the mine he takes and will declare to you.

en.L: All things whatever the Father has are {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}; because of this I said that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} takes from what is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} and will declare [it] to you.
en.B: Everything the Father has is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}. That is why I said that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will receive from what is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} and make it known to you.
en.R: Everything that belongs to the Father belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. That is why I said the Spirit will take what belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and tell it to you.

es.L: Todas las cosas que tiene el Padre son {{deity_pronoun:mías|Mías}}; por esto dije que toma de lo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}} y [lo] anunciará a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Todo lo que el Padre posee es {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}. Por eso dije que recibirá de lo que es {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}} y {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} dará a conocer.
es.R: Todo lo que pertenece al Padre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pertenece también a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Por eso dije que el Espíritu tomará lo que es {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}} y {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} contará.

fr.L: Toutes les choses que possède le Père sont {{deity_pronoun:miennes|Miennes}} ; à cause de cela, j’ai dit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prend de ce qui est {{deity_pronoun:mien|Mien}} et vous [l’]annoncera.
fr.B: Tout ce qu’a le Père est à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Voilà pourquoi j’ai dit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} recevra de ce qui est à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et vous le fera connaître.
fr.R: Tout ce qui appartient au Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartient aussi. C’est pour cela que j’ai dit que l’Esprit prendra ce qui est à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et vous le fera connaître.

sw.L: Vyote alivyo navyo Baba ni {{deity_pronoun:vyangu|Vyangu}}; kwa sababu hiyo nilisema kwamba anachukua katika yaliyo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atawatangazia.

vi.L: Mọi điều Cha có đều là của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; vì điều này {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lấy từ những gì thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và sẽ báo [điều đó] cho các con.
vi.B: Mọi sự Cha có đều là của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Vì thế {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ nhận từ những gì thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà cho các con biết.

ko.L: 아버지께서 가지신 것은 무엇이든지 다 내 것이다. 이 때문에 내가, 그분이 내 것에서 받으시고 너희에게 알려 주실 것이라고 말하였다.
ko.B: 아버지께서 가지신 것은 모두 내 것이다. 그래서 내가, 그분이 내 것을 받아서 너희에게 알려 주실 것이라고 말한 것이다.
ko.R: 아버지께 있는 것은 모두 나의 것이다. 그래서 내가, 성령께서 내 것을 가져다가 너희에게 알려 주실 것이라고 말한 것이다.

decisions.choice: all that the Father has is mine: the Son shares everything with the Father
decisions.reason: The Father has given all things into the Son's hands (3:35; 13:3), and in his prayer Jesus says, "all mine are yours, and yours are mine" (17:10). So when the Spirit takes from what is Jesus's, he makes known what is the Father's too: the Father, the Son and the Spirit work as one.

decisions.choice: he takes: a present tense where verse 14 has the future "he will take"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads the present λαμβάνει here; some manuscripts have the future, as in verse 14. The present may describe what the Spirit does as a settled pattern, or a future that is certain. The meaning is the same as verse 14. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: will receive (B); will take (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the future of verse 14, which this verse quotes (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the present.

decisions.choice: the Spirit
decisions.reason: Readable names the Spirit for "he", since the nearest person named is the Father.

decisions.choice: recibirá (B); el Espíritu tomará (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable repeat the future of verse 14, which this verse quotes (meaning decision m2); Literal keeps the present. Readable names the Spirit, since the nearest person named is the Father.
